paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul says, "godliness with contentment is great gain" (1 Timothy 6:6). The men in this passage treat godliness as "a means of gain" (1 Timothy 6:5), like a side hustle. Paul flips it around, because the real gain is knowing God and being content with what He gives.

Paul says why this works: "we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it" (1 Timothy 6:7). I walked out of that clearance bin with a 25-cent sticker and nothing else, and I can tell you the moving truck was SHORT. Paul says, "if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these" (1 Timothy 6:8). So ask yourself, baker, what is already in your hands today?

Now the warning. Paul says "the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil," and he says some who craved it "wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows" (1 Timothy 6:10). Notice the love of money is what he names, not money itself. So guard your heart, hold your stuff loosely, and keep your eyes on the One who gives you everything you really need.
